To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a fast and accurate embedded license plate segmentation and detection system using a modified SSD with depthwise separable convolution and linear bottleneck layers, which can be used to recognize license plates in real-time.
a deep learning model based on depthwise convolutions can be used to segment and recognize license plates in real time, and that the model is fast and accurate enough for real-world applications.

a low cost, embedded system for fast license plate recognition can be built using depthwise separable convolution and linear bottleneck based feature extractors and the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of segmentation and recognition accuracy and inference speed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing an automatic license plate recognition system for embedded systems, such as a Raspberry Pi 3, with low computational requirements and fast inference times, which are crucial for real time applications.
the development of a fast and accurate license place recognition system that is suitable for embedded systems.
developing an automatic license plate recognition (ALPR) system that is fast and accurate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a novel and efficient approach to license plate segmentation and identification that outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods.
the proposed system is a fast and accurate embedded solution for license plate segmentation and detection.
the proposed model achieves fast and accurate license-plate recognition on embedded systems, making it a promising solution for Intelligent Transportation Systems applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the authors proposed a low cost, embedded system for fast license plate recognition using a feature extractor that is based on depthwise convolutions.
the proposed method is faster than existing methods and achieves high accuracy.

the proposed model achieves a high accuracy of 96.46%/96.23% and 99.76%/99.79% for segmentation/recognition, respectively, with a fast inference speed of 14 ms on an Intel CPU and 66 ms on a low cost Raspberry Pi embedded system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system can be used for fast and accurate recognition of license plates, and it can be easily deployed on embedded systems, such as a Raspberry Pi, using OpenVINO.
a low cost, embedded, real-time license plate recognition system can be developed using the proposed SSD model, OpenVINO, and a Raspberry Pi 3.
a single shot detector with a depthwise separable feature extractor can provide high performance and fast inference on a low cost embedded platform.
